questions.q: In the four-band executive layout, what belongs in the top band?
options: The detail table of every open opportunity
Chart legends and footnotes
Filters (at most three), followed by a row of KPI tiles
The full list of report definitions
questions.explain: Filters and a KPI row come first so the VP sees the headline numbers before any detail. Detail tables sit at the bottom.

questions.q: A dashboard filter on Lead Source is added, but one chart does not change when it is used. What is the most likely cause?
options: The chart's source report does not include that field
Dashboards cannot be filtered
The chart is too large
Filters only work on tables
questions.explain: A dashboard filter only reaches components whose source report includes the filtered field, so check every component after adding a filter.

questions.q: Why should you choose the running user deliberately?
options: It changes the colors of the charts
It decides whether the dashboard can be scheduled
It controls how many components fit on the page
Viewers see the data that the running user can see, which may exceed their own access
questions.explain: With a fixed running user, every viewer sees that person's data. That suits an executive summary but must be a conscious choice.

questions.q: Which is the best reason to lean toward Tableau over a native dashboard for part of Project 3?
options: Native dashboards cannot show numbers
You need row-level blending across leads, opportunities and cases in a single view
Tableau is always faster to ship
The VP dislikes Salesforce
questions.explain: Native components each draw on one report. Row-level blending across objects is where Tableau tends to earn its place, though licences and org setup also matter.

questions.q: What is a sensible way to treat the questions your native dashboard cannot answer?
options: Hide them so the dashboard looks complete
Add 20 more components to compensate
Record them as evidence for the next tool, such as Tableau or CRM Analytics
Delete the dashboard
questions.explain: Limits are evidence, not failures. Ship the native dashboard, then log what it could not answer to justify the next step.
